messages.subject: Failed Milkweed Seed Bombs
messages.text:
Hello, 

 

 
 To whom it may concern, I wanted to ask if there is any guarantee for your products. The guide said not to plant before may but the seed bombs germinated in their seed bomb almost right away after I received them in April! 

 

 
So I planted them as your QR directed as soon as I noticed the germination but none of them grew afterwards. 

 

 
I am pretty disappointed in these seed bombs, they were expensive and in the end none of them worked, probably due to this early germination almost upon arrival (before the recommended plant date/time). 

 

 
Please advise how this can be rectified. 

 

 
Thank you, 

 

 

 
 

 
 Melissa Valente-Paterno, 

 
 M.Sc. Molecular Biology (Concordia University)

Research Assistant & Laboratory Manager

messages.subject: Re: Failed Milkweed Seed Bombs
messages.text:
Hi Melissa,

We've let this go on way too long, and I'm genuinely sorry for that.

On the seed bombs themselves: germination upon arrival is actually a good sign, not a defect, it means the seeds were healthy and the cold stratification worked. The challenge is that once seedlings sprout inside the bomb, they need to go into soil quickly or they run out of resources. Planting them right away, as you did, was exactly the right call. That said, very young milkweed seedlings are sensitive in those first few weeks (soil temperature, moisture, direct sun), and the cold snaps we still get in April likely made things harder than they should have been.

Either way, we want this to work for you. I'd like to send you a replacement order of seed bombs at no charge. Given where we are in the season now, the timing works well for getting them established before fall.

Is the shipping address on your original order still the right one to use? Once you confirm, I'll get the replacement out to you.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
